name: Directed Oxidation Lance DOL-3 'Rustmaker'
description: The DOL-3 projects a sustained stream of catalytically accelerated oxidation agents — a proprietary OUROBOROS ENERGY compound designated OX-7 — delivered in a superheated plasma carrier that allows the agent to penetrate surface coatings and begin attacking the metallic substrates beneath. Against standard materials, this is a moderate industrial cutting tool. Against cybernetic implants, it is a weapon of unusual cruelty: OX-7 is specifically formulated to attack the ferrous and titanium alloys most commonly used in structural cybernetic components, causing rapid surface degradation that generates heat as a byproduct. An implant struck by the Rustmaker does not simply fail — it heats from within as its structural integrity deteriorates, causing thermal burns to surrounding tissue from the inside outward while simultaneously seizing joints and locking mechanical augmentations in place.
specifications:
form factor: Heavy two-handed configuration, 920mm length, with rear-mounted OX-7 canister and integrated plasma excitation chamber
effective range: Up to 12 meters sustained stream; 6 meters for full catalytic effect
power source: Integrated plasma coil, powered by weapon's own battery cell; OX-7 canister provides approximately 15 seconds of sustained fire
weight: 4.8 kg (with full OX-7 canister)
stream temperature: 400–600°C at plasma carrier exit
OX-7 catalytic onset: 0.8 seconds on contact with target alloy
effect on unaugmented targets: Severe thermal burns — effective but non-specific
effect on cybernetic targets: Structural degradation, thermal seizure of mechanical components, internal thermal burns from implant heat generation
canister replacement time: 12 seconds
tactical_use: The Rustmaker originated as an industrial tool for controlled demolition of cybernetic infrastructure — primarily used by OUROBOROS ENERGY crews decommissioning old implant manufacturing lines. The weaponized variant entered black market circulation when operators realized its unique effectiveness against heavily augmented combatants who had essentially traded biological vulnerability for cybernetic vulnerability. In combat, it is used at close range against targets whose subdermal plating defeats conventional ammunition — the oxidation agent bypasses surface hardening by attacking material composition rather than structure. It is a last-resort weapon in most operational contexts due to its weight, limited ammunition, and the difficulty of operating it in enclosed spaces.
cultural_context: The Rustmaker carries significant symbolic weight in GLMZ's political landscape. Anti-augmentation extremist groups have adopted it as an ideological weapon, and incidents of its use against augmentation clinics and prosthetics workshops have made it a charged symbol. For heavily augmented individuals, the threat of the Rustmaker represents a specific existential horror — not just death, but the betrayal of the body they have built, their augmentations turned against them. OUROBOROS ENERGY has faced significant reputational damage from the weaponized variant's association with extremist violence, despite their insistence that the industrial variant serves legitimate purposes.
known_users: Operators working anti-cyborg contracts for unknown clients
OUROBOROS ENERGY security teams (industrial variant, occasionally deployed in facility defense)
A bounty hunter known as 'Patina' who specializes in cybernetic fugitive retrieval and uses the DOL-3 to disable augmented targets non-lethally through implant seizure
story_hooks: A series of attacks on augmentation clinics using Rustmakers has been attributed to a known extremist group — but the OX-7 compound used is from a batch that was never sold commercially, pointing back to OUROBOROS ENERGY itself.

A character's critical cybernetic limb has been partially oxidized in an attack — it still functions, but structural integrity is compromised and failure is inevitable without replacement they can't afford.
A weapons dealer is offering DOL-3 units at suspiciously low prices in bulk — someone is trying to flood a specific district before an event, and figuring out which event is the urgent question.

OUROBOROS ENERGY hires operators to recover a stolen industrial DOL-3 unit before it can be converted to its weaponized configuration — but the thieves turn out to have more sympathetic motives than expected.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist industrial projector weapon with a distinctly asymmetrical profile—heavy rear-loaded design suggests a flamethrower-adjacent device, but the front assembly is more clinical and precise. The nozzle cluster sits elevated above a reinforced grip assembly, giving it an almost praying mantis appearance. Functional and threatening, with no aesthetic pretense.
physical_description.dimensions: 920mm overall length, 180mm width at widest point (canister bulge), 140mm height at nozzle assembly
physical_description.weight_description: Genuinely hefty—4.8kg requires committed two-handed control. Feels front-heavy due to canister positioning, demanding braced stance or mounting for sustained use. The weight distribution fatigues the arms quickly in extended engagement.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with brushed titanium alloy heat-dispersal shrouding around the nozzle assembly. Canister body is stainless steel with visible seam-welding.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with oxidized steel accents. The nozzle shroud shows intentional heat-scorching and discoloration from test fires. Canister bears faint factory mill marks and light surface rust in stress-concentration areas.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, with brushed steel nozzle shroud and dark anodized aluminum grip panels. The OX-7 canister is unmarked stainless steel with minimal branding.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubberized polymer with embossed hexagonal pattern for purchase; dual secondary grips positioned for two-handed control. Some wear from industrial handling; residual oxidation stains in grip crevices suggest field use.
distinctive_features: Tri-nozzle plasma excitation cluster at muzzle—three offset apertures arranged in triangular pattern for stream coherence
Rear-mounted OX-7 canister with pressure-release valve and gauge (analog mechanical readout, not digital)
Integrated plasma coil housing visible through reinforced viewport window on right side—faint blue-white glow when powered
Cable conduit running from battery chamber to excitation assembly, industrial-grade shielded wiring
Canister quick-release lever with wear-polished engagement surfaces
Exhaust vents along upper barrel—scorched aluminum with internal discoloration from heat cycling
Faint residue staining on nozzle shroud suggesting OX-7 compound exposure or spillage during maintenance
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: SERPENTINE DATA CENTERS stamped in small serif font on left side of canister, below pressure gauge. Serial number etched on rear of polymer grip. Faded OUROBOROS ENERGY logo on canister shoulder (original industrial variant marking). Black-market weaponized variants show obliterated or filed-down manufacturer stamps.
physical_description.condition_typical: Industrial variants appear clean and well-maintained with minimal external wear. Black-market weaponized variants show battle-scarring: scuffed polymer, scratched coil viewport, residue buildup around nozzle, and stress marks on quick-release mechanisms from repeated canister swaps in field conditions.
